cohort: 10,923 children of multiparous women in Rhode Island who were term, singleton births without congenital anomalies, born between 2014-2017
finding: Compared to repeated cesarean delivery, both vaginal birth after cesarean delivery and repeated vaginal birth were not associated with differences in educational outcomes.
mod_finding: The study found that neither vaginal birth after cesarean delivery nor repeat vaginal birth were associated with differences in educational outcomes compared to repeat cesarean delivery.
